title: Green Heart Emoji 💚 Meaning: Nature, Envy or Fandom?
description: The green heart emoji 💚 can mean love of nature, healthy living, Irish pride, a favorite team or K-pop group, and now and then jealousy. Here's how to tell.
summary: The 💚 green heart emoji usually means affection tied to something green: nature, the environment, healthy living, Ireland, or a team or fandom whose color is green. Between people it is a friendly, low-key heart. A few use it for jealousy, playing on “green with envy.”
meaning: More than any other heart, the green one takes its meaning from a topic. Under a hiking photo it is love of the outdoors. On a post about recycling or climate it signals environmental commitment. Beside a salad, a smoothie or a plant-based recipe it means healthy or vegan. Around March 17 it stands for St. Patrick's Day and Irish heritage. The emoji is doing color work first and emotional work second.

When it is aimed at a person, 💚 is mild. It expresses fondness and good wishes, a little cooler than yellow and far from red. Some friends use it as their assigned color. In a romantic conversation it tends to be read as casual or friendly unless the couple has made it their own, so it is not the heart to pick for a first “I like you.”

The jealousy meaning exists but is smaller than its reputation. English speakers know “green with envy” and the “green-eyed monster,” so a pointed 💚 under a friend's vacation photo can mean “I'm jealous,” nearly always in a teasing way. Used seriously about a partner, it is rare. If someone intends envy, the caption generally says so.

Fan communities give it another layer. Supporters of clubs and countries that play in green post it on match days. In K-pop, NCT fans use 💚 as a fandom marker because green is the group's color. It also appears in mental health awareness posts, where a green ribbon is the established symbol, and in Ramadan and Eid greetings, since green is widely associated with Islam.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: As a sign-off between friends it is easygoing: “see you Saturday 💚.” It suits people who find red too intense and want something calmer than yellow. If a contact always sends green, it is probably their favorite color. Read alone as a reply, it means roughly “love that” or “thanks.”

contexts.label: In captions
contexts.body: Nature and wellness content relies on it. Forest trails, houseplants, matcha, farmers' market hauls and garden updates all get a green heart, often with 🌿 or 🌱. Sustainable brands and vegan restaurants use it almost as a logo. In these posts it tells you the subject, not the poster's feelings toward you.

contexts.label: In sports and fandom
contexts.body: Match-day timelines fill with 💚 for teams in green, frequently combined with a second heart for the other kit color, such as 💚🤍. Music fans do the same for artists with a green era or official color. Seeing dozens of green hearts under one post usually points to a fandom, not a romance.

contexts.label: On holidays
contexts.body: St. Patrick's Day brings a flood of green hearts with shamrocks and Irish flags. At Christmas it pairs with ❤️ for the traditional red-and-green scheme. Earth Day posts use it with a globe. Each occasion gives the same emoji a different, obvious meaning.

examples.meaning: Celebrating St. Patrick's Day and Irish identity.
Affection for houseplants; the heart matches the subject.
Pride in a plant-based lifestyle milestone.

examples.text: Thanks for checking in on me 💚
What a win, come on you boys in green 💚
examples.meaning: Support for a team that plays in green.

combos.meaning: Irish pride or St. Patrick's Day greetings.
Care for the planet; Earth Day and environmental messages.
Christmas colors, or the colors of a flag or team in red and green.
Healthy eating, clean living or a vegan meal.

confusedWith.difference: 🍀 means luck. People combine it with the green heart on St. Patrick's Day, but they do different jobs: the clover wishes good fortune, while 💚 expresses affection or allegiance.
💛 is the standard friendship heart with a happy, sunny tone and almost no thematic baggage. 💚 is cooler and usually connected to a subject such as nature, health or a team.
🤢 is the green emoji for disgust or sickness. Someone joking about envy might reach for either, but the green heart stays affectionate while the green face says something is revolting.

avoid: Do not use it as your main romantic heart with someone new, who may read it as casual or even as a hint of jealousy.
Avoid assuming envy when you receive it; in most messages it is friendly or topical.
Check which team wears green before posting it under a rivalry match.
design: A solid heart in a medium to bright green, sharing the red heart's outline on every platform. Apple's version is a glossy grass green, and other vendors range from lime to a deeper emerald. It was part of the original 2010 emoji set, alongside the yellow, blue and purple hearts, and has kept the same simple design since.

faqs.q: What does 💚 mean from a girl?
faqs.a: Usually friendliness, or a match to whatever you were talking about: plants, food, a team. If she uses green hearts everywhere, it is her color. It is not a typical way to flirt, so look for other signals before drawing conclusions.

faqs.q: What does 💚 mean from a guy?
faqs.a: Commonly a casual, safe heart. Men often pick green or blue with friends because those colors feel less romantic. It may also be sports-related. If he likes you, it will show in what he writes more than in this emoji.

faqs.q: Does the green heart mean jealousy?
faqs.a: Sometimes, as a joke built on “green with envy.” It is usually obvious from context, for example a comment on a friend's enviable photo. Most green hearts have nothing to do with jealousy.

It most often identifies fans of NCT, whose official color is a shade of green. Fans place it in usernames, comments and concert posts. Other groups have their own heart colors, so the green heart works as a quick badge of belonging.

faqs.q: Is the green heart linked to mental health?
faqs.a: Yes, loosely. A green ribbon is the recognized symbol for mental health awareness, so people posting about that subject often add 💚. In that setting it expresses support and solidarity.
